title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

text.how-you-fall: You fall by tending. Gi is the garden soil, the field that feeds everything planted in it. You notice what someone needs before they do: the snack, the charger, the reassurance after a bad day at work. Caring for them is how you realize you like them, often after you've already been doing it for weeks. Your love is warm, attentive and incredibly practical. Partners feel looked after in a way that's rare. The danger is that you can confuse being needed with being loved. You might fall for people who need a lot of tending, because being useful feels safe, and slowly end up doing the emotional housework for two. Ask yourself early: if I stopped helping, would they still want me here? With the right person, the answer is an obvious yes.
text.flirting: You flirt like a really good host. You check if they're comfortable, you remember they don't like spicy food, you send them the article about the thing they mentioned. People feel calm and cared for around you, and that quiet warmth is extremely attractive. You're also funnier than people expect, with an earthy, self-deprecating humour that sneaks up on them. What you don't do is make the first obvious move. You'd rather create the perfect conditions and wait for them to step in, like planting seeds and hoping for rain. Sometimes it works. Sometimes the other person thinks you're just nice to everyone. Try being the rain once. Send the text that says "I'd like to see you again, just us." The garden will forgive you for being bold.
text.attachment: Your pattern leans anxious, mostly in your head. You overthink. A message left on read can turn into a full internal investigation: did I say too much, was I boring, are they losing interest? You often worry quietly and keep giving, hoping care will secure the bond. When things are good, you're a gentle, loyal and deeply reassuring partner, the person who makes home feel like home. The tricky part is that you rarely ask for reassurance directly, so you end up both anxious and helpful at the same time, which is tiring. The growth step for you is asking for what you give. You offer comfort constantly. Let yourself say, "I'm feeling a bit insecure, can you remind me we're good?" It's not needy. It's fair.
text.jealousy: Your jealousy comes dressed as worry. You don't think "I'm jealous," you think "I'm not enough." When your person spends time with someone fun, attractive or impressive, you quietly compare and find yourself lacking. Then you over-function: more care, more favours, more effort to be indispensable. Your trigger is feeling replaceable. Because you give so much, the idea that someone else could step in and be liked more easily feels unfair, and it is a little unfair, in your head. The answer isn't to give more. It's to let your partner show you you're chosen. Ask a direct question instead of competing in silence. And notice: people don't stay with you because you're useful. They stay because you make life feel softer.
text.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you mother your partners. You manage their laundry, their schedule, their emotional state and their relationship with their own mum, and then wonder why the romance feels like childcare. Second flag: martyr mode. You quietly do everything and quietly keep score, then feel unappreciated when nobody notices the score exists. Third: overthinking. You can create an entire breakup in your head out of one slightly short reply and be sad about it before anything actually happens. None of this comes from a bad place. It comes from caring too much and asking too little. Stop fertilizing people who don't plant anything back. You deserve someone who brings you snacks, too.
text.what-you-need: You need someone who gives back without being asked. A partner who notices your effort and returns it, who makes you tea when you're the one who's tired, who plans the date for once. You need warmth and steadiness more than excitement. Grand gestures are nice, but what really reassures you is consistency: the same goodnight text, the same easy affection, the same calm answer when you ask if everything is okay. You also need encouragement to take up space. You're used to supporting other people's plans, so someone who asks "and what do you want?" is quietly life-changing for you. The best match makes you feel like the garden and the person sitting in it, not just the ground everyone walks on.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you love like a garden. Patient, nurturing, everyone around you just grows.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also love like an unpaid personal assistant. With overtime.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're so caring! People feel completely at home with you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you're overthinking that two-word reply right now. I can tell.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Ask for the care you give. You're allowed to be looked after too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Being needed is not the same as being loved. Know the difference.

spring.intro: Spring is Wood's season, and Wood controls Earth. A spring-born Gi Earth is the field at planting time, with every seed asking for space, so you learned to make room for others early. In love you are nurturing and practical, and you notice what a partner needs before they say it. The pressure of the season can make you accommodating to a fault. You let the other person set the pace, the plans and the tone, then feel overlooked and are not sure why. Fire, your resource, steadies you: warmth, appreciation, your own goals given equal sunlight. Good soil is not just there to be used. It is what makes the garden possible.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Gi, you said 'whatever you want' four times this week. What do you want?

summer.intro: With Fire in command and Fire feeding Earth, a summer-born Gi Earth is warm, fertile ground. You are a deeply caring lover with real confidence in your instincts. You make a home of any relationship: snacks in the car, a playlist for their bad day, gentle advice delivered at exactly the right moment. With so much support behind you, the risk is over-managing. You can start organising your partner's life because you can see what would help, and help turns into control without either of you noticing. Metal is the element you produce, and in love it means clean boundaries. Offer care, then let them choose whether to take it. That choice is intimacy too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Gi, your care is a gift. Gifts don't come with instructions. Let them choose.

autumn.intro: Autumn is Metal's season, and Earth produces Metal. A Gi Earth born in autumn is the field after harvest: generous, tired and still giving. You love by producing results. You remember the details, solve the problems, make the relationship run smoothly, and you are proud of that. But a field that keeps giving without rest gets thin. You can slip into being your partner's assistant rather than their lover, then quietly resent it. Your resource is Fire, which means delight, compliments, plans made purely for your enjoyment. Let someone take care of you without having earned it first. Love does not need to be a fair trade every single week.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Gi, you planned their birthday, their mum's and the dog's. Who's planning yours?

winter.intro: Winter is Water's season, and Earth controls Water. A winter-born Gi Earth is cold, damp ground, full of potential but waiting for warmth. You are thoughtful and private in love. You prefer to watch a person for a long time before you trust them, and you hold a surprising amount of emotion under a calm surface. Because the season is cold, you can doubt whether you are interesting enough, so you stay helpful instead of being vulnerable. Fire is what your chart craves: someone who seeks you out, who is playful, who makes plans with obvious excitement. When someone warms you, you become the richest soil in the garden. Let yourself be wanted.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Gi, you don't have to be useful to be wanted. Some people just want you.

strength.strong: A strong Gi Earth is rich, deep soil with a lot of opinions about the garden. With plenty of Earth and Fire behind you, you are nurturing, capable and certain you know what is best for the people you love. Your blind spot is overpowering through care: managing their schedule, fixing their problems, offering advice nobody asked for. It comes from love, and it can still feel like supervision. Let your partner struggle with something without rescuing them. Ask, 'do you want help or company?' The answer may surprise you, and the relationship will finally have room to breathe.
strength.weak: A weak Gi Earth is thin soil trying to grow a whole orchard. With little Earth or Fire support, you give care constantly and rarely receive it back in the same measure. You adapt to every partner's needs, apologise for having your own, and feel guilty when you rest. Your blind spot is shrinking into a helpful role: the reliable one, the easygoing one, the one who never complains. Underneath, resentment builds quietly. Practise receiving. Accept the compliment, the gift, the offer of dinner without bargaining. Love is not only what you provide. It is also what you allow.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might wait for the other person to make the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practising small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard, flirt boldly and feel everything at full volume. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colours and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practising clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labelled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard, fast and loudly. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
